Good — we'll mock an interviewer for a financial analyst role. Here's the first question; answer as you would in the room, and I'll score it and give one concrete improvement before the next question.

"Walk me through your resume — highlight the parts that make you a strong fit for a financial analyst role and one weakness you're working on."

Why: Your answer names what you would do (action) but not the context, your role, or any result. Interviewers want a short STAR: what problem you faced, what you specifically did, and the measurable outcome.
Rewrite (2–3 sentences) you can use now — fill the [brackets] with your true details:
"At [Company], we needed a monthly forecast after revenue fell two quarters in a row (Situation). I led the build of a three‑statement model starting from revenue drivers (price × volume) and ran scenario checks against three public comps; I automated the scenario runs in [tool/process you used] so the team could update inputs weekly (Action). That model reduced forecast variance by [X%] and helped the CFO decide to delay a planned hire, saving roughly $[Y]K over the next quarter (Result)."
One concrete improvement for your next answer: always attach a number or time frame to the result (X%, $Y, weeks reduced).

You asked for an honest score — 2/10 stands. Short reasons, then one clear next step.

- Missing S (situation): no context or problem.  
- Missing A (your specific action beyond a generic task): you said what to build but not what you personally did to make it work.  
- Missing R (result): no metric, timeframe, or outcome.  
- Lacked tools/scale: didn’t say toolset, team size, or frequency.

You don't have any Lincoln International materials or applications on file yet. The one step that starts this: paste the job posting or the recruiter’s interview schedule (rounds, who you meet, timing) so I can tailor answers and the questions to them.

Below is a focused, role-specific final-round prep for an Analyst at Lincoln International. I assumed a typical middle‑market M&A analyst scope (accounting, valuation, modelling, deal work). If any assumption is wrong, paste the posting or the recruiter’s schedule and I’ll adjust.
1) 60‑second “Tell me about yourself” (structure + draft)
- Structure: 1 sentence current role & what you do → 1 sentence 1–2 relevant accomplishments with numbers → 1 sentence why Lincoln and what you bring.
- Draft (~60s): “I’m [Your current title] at [Company], where I run financial analysis and build models to support transactions and strategic decisions. Over the last [X years/months] I led financial modelling and due diligence on [number] transactions, improved forecast accuracy by [X%] and supported a [size] deal from analysis through close. I want to move into full‑cycle M&A work — Lincoln’s middle‑market focus and cross‑border deal flow match my experience and let me contribute immediately with fast, accurate modelling and client-facing clarity.”
Action: replace bracketed items with your facts and time it to ~60s.
2) Three STAR stories to prepare (2–3 short sentences each)
- Team win: Situation → your specific action → quantifiable result. Example: “We needed to close a cross‑border sale in six weeks; I rebuilt the target’s model, identified $X of synergies and prepared the buyer Q&A deck, which shortened negotiation cycles and helped the deal close on time.” Add exact deal count/size or % time saved.
- Hard problem (technical): “Revenue recognition was inconsistent across product lines; I reconciled accounting schedules to cash, corrected a $Y misstatement risk, and updated projections so buyers could underwrite the business reliably.” Add outcomes (audit sign‑off, buyer confidence, deal progress).
- Failure → learning: “I missed a key assumption that affected valuation; I owned it, re‑ran sensitivities, and implemented a model checklist that cut similar corrections by Z%.” Say what changed (process, checks) and the measurable improvement.
3) Accounting & modelling drills (talk these in one sentence each)
- How the three statements connect: Net income flows to retained earnings; adjust net income for non‑cash items and working capital to get operating cash flow; investing/financing flow to cash on the balance sheet.
- Working capital definition & DCF relevance: Current assets − current liabilities; changes affect free cash flow and therefore valuation.
- EBITDA limits: Ignores capex, working capital, taxes and debt service, so it can overstate true cash available.
4) Valuation questions to rehearse (short, structured answers)
- Walk through a DCF in five steps: project free cash flows → choose discount rate (WACC) → compute terminal value → discount FCFs + terminal to PV → get enterprise value then subtract debt/add cash to get equity value.
- Choosing terminal growth & WACC: Terminal growth conservative (~long‑term GDP/inflation); WACC from market risk premium, beta, capital structure — justify each input.

5) Quick technical practice (timed prompts)
- Valuation (90s each): build a 3‑year mini DCF from a simple profit stream; explain when you’d use precedent transactions vs. comps.
6) Fit / behavioural prep (two-line answers)
- Why Lincoln: Focus on their middle‑market M&A strength and cross‑border reach; say how that matches the deals you want to own and the skills you’ll bring.
- Why you: Emphasise technical modelling, deal exposure you’ve had, speed and client communication.
7) Questions to ask them (pick 2–3)
- “How are analyst responsibilities structured on a typical sell‑side engagement — what do analysts own day‑to‑day?”
- “What recent deal or sector has the team found most strategically interesting, and what skills do successful analysts demonstrate on that work?”
- Logistics if not stated: rounds, who I’ll meet, expected timing for decisions, and whether I should expect a modelling/case test.
8) Final‑round checklist (do these now)
- Confirm time, time zone, link or address and interviewers; ask recruiter now if not given.
- Ask whether to bring a laptop or spreadsheet for a modelling test.
- Test video, mic, screen‑sharing; prepare a one‑page cheat sheet with 3 stories, 5 technical bullets, and 2 questions.
- Have an Excel file with a clean, simple model (3‑year projections, simple DCF tabs) ready to share.

9) Mock offer
- If you want a timed mock, say “mock me for Analyst at Lincoln International” and I’ll start with the first question immediately.
Next step: paste the job posting or the recruiter’s interview schedule (who you meet, the format and timing) so I can tailor the stories, the technical drills and produce a timed mock. Is that coming now?

Here is exactly what I will put into the first application card, field by field, and what I will need from you for each. I’ll use the posting’s wording where required and only confirmed facts you’ve given me or the items you supply now.
1) Target posting (read-only)
- What goes there: company name, job title, location, posting link and the posting’s internal id.
- Where it comes from: the posting you picked.
- What I need: nothing else from you for this field.

2) Resume PDF (required)
- What goes there: a single PDF resume created from your confirmed facts and the resume text you paste or confirm. The file will be named and a short private link will be included on the card.
- What I need: paste your resume now (I will read it and show two quick edits to improve fit) or confirm a saved resume contact/name+email.
3) Short cover note / quick message (optional but recommended, under 120 words)
- What goes there: one-paragraph note to the hiring team tailored to the posting. I’ll include one sentence on why you want the role and one sentence tying a relevant achievement to the job’s top requirement. Anything I don’t have will be left in [brackets].
- What I need: one-sentence reason you want this role (or I’ll use a sensible default) and one achievement (preferably with a metric) to cite, or tell me to leave it blank.
4) Work authorization / sponsorship answer (if the posting asks)
- What goes there: the exact question(s) from the employer and your answer copied verbatim from your confirmed facts.
- What I need: confirm your work authorization now if not already on file (e.g., US citizen, green card, needs sponsorship).

5) Location / remote preference (if the posting asks)
- What goes there: your current city and the posting’s location options (onsite/hybrid/remote) as they appear; I’ll mark whether you accept remote or relocation based on your confirmed preference.
- What I need: confirm your current location and whether you accept remote work or relocation if not already confirmed.
6) Title / role as presented
- What goes there: the role title as it will appear on the application (by default I use the posting title).
- What I need: tell me if you prefer a different phrasing.

7) Contact info for the application form (name and email)
- What goes there: name and email exactly as you provide them now (I will save them and use them on the resume and form).
- What I need: supply the exact name and email to use at top of resume and on the form.
8) Phone number (if the employer requests it)
- What goes there: the phone you give me, verbatim; if you prefer not to include a phone I will leave it blank (some forms require it).
- What I need: phone number now only if you want it included.

9) LinkedIn / portfolio URLs (if requested)
- What goes there: the exact URLs you supply, verbatim.
- What I need: the profile or portfolio links you want included, or say “none.”
10) Screening question answers (yes/no, short text)
- What goes there: each employer screening question and your short answers. I’ll copy the posting’s exact question and slot your confirmed facts or bracketed prompts where something is missing.
- What I need: confirm any items I mark in [brackets] (for example, years of experience in a specific skill).

11) Short-answer prompts (resume summary, “why us”, three-sentence answers)
- What goes there: tailored 1–3 sentence answers per prompt, using only your confirmed facts and the achievement you provided. Missing pieces will be bracketed.
- What I need: supply any bracketed phrases if you want a specific line included.
12) Attachments (certifications, transcripts, work samples)
- What goes there: any files you upload or tell me to attach, named exactly as you give them.
- What I need: upload or paste the names of any files you want attached, or say “none.”

13) Desired salary / pay expectations (if asked)
- What goes there: I’ll copy the posting’s stated pay if included; if not, I’ll place your confirmed salary range or leave it bracketed.
- What I need: give a pay range if you want one placed and the posting doesn’t list pay.
14) Availability / earliest start date
- What goes there: your confirmed earliest start date or the bracketed placeholder.
- What I need: confirm your earliest start date if not on file.

15) Consent / signature checkbox
- What goes there: a clear line that you must approve sending the card. I will not mark this checked. The card waits for your approval in your browser/extension before anything goes to the employer.
- What I need: you must open the application card in your extension and click approve/send.
16) Private recruiter note (optional)
- What goes there: an optional 1–2 sentence private note to the recruiter (for example: “Available for interviews evenings this week”).
- What I need: provide a 1–2 sentence note or say “none.”

17) Audit trail and sources (read-only)
- What goes there: timestamp and the source of each field (posting text, your confirmed fact, or bracketed).
- What I need: nothing; this is generated automatically.

What I will not do
- I will not submit the application without your approval on the application card.
- I will not invent facts or add unconfirmed information to the resume or application fields.
Next step: paste the posting link (or tell me the job title and company) and paste your resume text now so I can read it and prepare the application card with any bracketed items highlighted for you to confirm. Is that the posting and resume you want me to start with?
